bullets.title: Semis/Tech selloff: broad premarket weakness with SOXX -7%, momentum fragility exposed
bullets.body: A ~10% drop in the Korean KOSPI (leveraged ETF unwind) rippled into US semis, with SOXX down 7%, CRDO -8.4%, CRWV -7.8%, GLW -7.1%, AAOI -7.0%, LITE -6.7%, and CIEN -6.0% in premarket. S&P futures were down 1.4% and Nasdaq futures -3.0%, with DRAM down 12% premarket. Multiple strategists flagged levered ETF short gamma at record -$18bn/1% move (¾ benchmarked to semis/NDX/tech) as an accelerant, and a COR1M correlation measure at 6.64 historically associated with 2-3% S&P pullbacks within two weeks.

bullets.title: AI momentum crowding at extremes; Mag 7 = 32% of S&P, breadth narrowest since 1990
bullets.body: Top 10 S&P constituents account for 37% of index market cap, exceeding Dot-Com era peaks, with Mag 7 alone at 32%. Only 17% of stocks are driving 80% of YTD returns—the narrowest breadth since 1990. Historical data suggests concentration alone doesn't signal imminent reversal, but downside risk is concentrated in the highest-appreciation stocks; a derivative hedge cited is MTUM July 17th 320/270 put spread ~$7.

bullets.title: Tech structural deterioration: MSFT at 6.5-year relative low, GOOGL joins bearish TREND list
bullets.body: MSFT's technical score is at 0 across all timeframes, below both 50- and 200-day MAs with the 200-day still sloping lower; a break below 350 implies downside risk to 250. GOOGL joined Hedgeye's bearish TREND breakdown list after a -6% session on frontier lab concerns and open-source share gains. The tech sector is showing a 37-day negative advance/decline streak—the longest in 24+ years, surpassing 2007 and 2012.

bullets.title: US manufacturing PMI hits 4-year high at 55.7; expansion expected through 1H 2027
bullets.body: S&P Global Manufacturing PMI rose 0.6pts to 55.7 in June, the eleventh consecutive month of expansion, with new orders accelerating to 57.5%. Composite regional capex plans rose 3.2ppts m/m to the strongest since 2022. Input/output prices decelerated with tariff pass-through nearing completion, and oil is no longer a headwind; analysts expect manufacturing expansion to continue at least into 1H 2027, broadening beyond AI/tech buildout.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex on trillion-dollar trajectory; server TAM surging to $1.3T by CY27
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises CY26 server market TAM to $800B (+82% YoY) with CY27 projected at $1.3T. TSMC CoWoS remains the gating AI supply bottleneck with capacity rising to 200k wpm by YE27; NVDA expected to consume 1,222k CoWoS units in 2027 (+57% YoY). A single AI server consumes ~440k MLCCs (10-15x traditional servers), with channel MLCC pricing +200-300% since 1Q26 as capacity grows only 10-15% annually. Hyperscaler capex expectations are moving higher with AI spending on a trillion-dollar annual trajectory.

bullets.title: MU earnings tomorrow: short gamma overhang largest after SK Hynix; retail buyers undeterred
bullets.body: MU has the second-most short gamma in the US after SK Hynix, with levered ETF positioning making it a flashpoint for tomorrow's post-close print. Retail has been buying at $6bn/day with MU in the top 10 most-purchased names YTD, and ~20% of accounts have <10% AI exposure supporting potential dip-buying. Citi models 6%/5% EPS upside for the May/August quarters; separately MU was already up +7% earlier in the session on an AI lab supply deal.

bullets.title: AVGO bull case: custom silicon revenue potential $250-300B FY28 on XPV-financed deployments
bullets.body: Wolfe Research sees AVGO custom revenue reaching $250-300B in FY28 if XPV financing with Apollo drives 15GW of incremental OpenAI/Anthropic deployments, with $10-15B/GW content range for Google/Anthropic builds. MRVL is selectively raising pricing with CY26 enterprise data guidance of 85% YoY growth treated as a floor. Tokyo Electron expects CY27 WFE spending floor ~$170B with $185B a reasonable target.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness under Warsh + tightening excess liquidity flagged as near-term equity risk
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag Fed's shift to a more hawkish stance under Warsh—with reduced transparency—as a material risk to momentum-heavy portfolios. Excess liquidity has turned negative for the first time since 2021, and funding spreads have widened to their highest since 2024. Morgan Stanley notes US front-end rates expected to be the noisiest in a generation, with the S&P-to-gold ratio reflecting confidence in Fed credibility under Warsh leadership.

bullets.title: Goldman PCE preview: Core PCE stays elevated at 3.2% through Dec 2026 on AI and energy passthrough
bullets.body: Goldman forecasts core PCE inflation at 3.2% by December 2026, slowing to 2.2% by December 2027 as AI-related price pressures and energy passthrough effects fade. H2 GDP growth expected at 2%; consumer spending growth constrained at 1.5% due to limited real income growth.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMI still in contraction at 49.5%; CPI model points to 5.1% by August
bullets.body: Eurozone June composite PMI rose only 0.9ppts to 49.5%, with services at 48.9% and manufacturing at 51.3%. Headline CPI is forecast to accelerate to 5.1% YoY by August, Bund yields hit 2.91% (highest since 2011), and markets price at least one more ECB hike despite weak activity.

bullets.title: Nuclear power accelerating: DOE $17.5B loan program for 10 AP1000 reactors; CEG/WMT 30-yr PPA
bullets.body: DOE announced a $17.5B low-interest loan program for utilities to finance 10 Westinghouse AP1000 reactors with seven utilities signing LOIs. Separately, CEG announced a 176MW, 30-year PPA with Walmart beginning 2029 for the Dresden nuclear facility, and MDU signed a 430MW data center campus service agreement with APLD in North Dakota.

bullets.title: SPX approaching gamma flip at 7320; VIX >18.83 would trigger TREND breakout
bullets.body: OPCO flags the S&P approaching a negative gamma flip level at 7320, which would act as an accelerant for volatility if breached. Separately Hedgeye notes VIX >18.83 is a TREND breakout level where gamma could flip negative. Technical strategist Craig Johnson flags QQQ support at $720/$695/$685 and SMH support at $620/$616/$612/$600.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 at all-time highs, outperforming S&P by 11.9% YTD; small cap fair value implies +30% upside
bullets.body: Russell 2000 is up 21.1% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500 by 11.9%, with AI buildout beneficiaries (Cap Goods, Semis, Tech Hardware, Energy) driving 13ppts of that return. Small cap 1Q earnings beat rate of 72% exceeded the long-term median of 63.5%, and small cap multiples remain depressed vs large caps with fair value implying +30% upside if the multiple spread normalizes. A technical target of 3200 (+6%) is cited.

bullets.title: India eliminates bond withholding tax; FAR bonds join GBI-EM Narrow index at 10% weight
bullets.body: India's government eliminated all withholding and capital gains taxes on Indian government bonds for foreign investors effective June 30, 2026. FAR bonds will be phased into the GBI-EM Narrow diversified index starting July 31, reaching a 10% terminal weight, reducing index yields by 2bps and adding 0.12 years of duration. Romania (-330bps), Hungary (-277bps), and Peru (-210bps) face material weight reductions.

bullets.title: AI disintermediation raising valuation uncertainty for incumbent software: CRM, ORCL risk cited
bullets.body: Liberty Mutual CIO warns that 30-year credit in Salesforce and Oracle is much riskier given AI-driven uncertainty, arguing the next trillion-dollar companies may never adopt Salesforce and that even cash-cow businesses deserve lower multiples. UBS separately notes WMT's acquisition of Vibe.co signals a retail media arms race with AMZN, while ACN's 25% selloff and 20-year valuation low (2Y forward P/E 8.5x) reflects excessive AI disintermediation fear that a $2B buyback is designed to counter.

bullets.title: Social media platform liability + AI regulation risk rising: KIDS Act advances bipartisan
bullets.body: House Energy and Commerce reached bipartisan agreement to advance the Kids Internet and Digital Safety (KIDS) Act, with ongoing litigation risk for META, SNAP, and GOOGL (YouTube) around mental health impacts following a bellwether school district settlement. Section 230 reform momentum is building, with open questions about whether immunity extends to AI-generated outputs and federal AI legislation timelines.

bullets.title: QCOM Investor Day and MLCC super-cycle among key near-term catalysts to watch
bullets.body: QCOM hosts its Investor Day at 14:15 ET on June 24th, expected to focus on data center offerings and mid-term strategic targets. Separately, Morgan Stanley identifies an MLCC super-cycle as a structural supply crunch driven by AI servers consuming ~440k units each (10-15x traditional), with channel pricing up 200-300% since 1Q26 against capacity growth of only 10-15% annually through 2030.

bullets.title: Internet sector rebounds with macro fears easing; AMZN/GOOGL/META at relative valuation discounts
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley rates the internet sector Attractive as growth rebounds, with GOOGL at 25x '26E EPS (-3% vs TTM avg), AMZN at 26x (-19% vs TTM avg), and META at 18x (-28% vs TTM avg). BKNG was +4% and RDDT +8% on the session. GOOGL's -5-6% session was attributed to concerns over frontier lab status loss and open-source AI gaining share.

bullets.title: HOOD $2B convert priced; crypto/miner complex down 5-6% on dilution concerns
bullets.body: Robinhood priced a $2.0B convertible note offering, sending shares down 5.9% in premarket. The crypto/miner complex followed: BTDR -5.7%, WULF -5.2%, CORZ -4.5%, reflecting broader risk-off in high-beta momentum names.

bullets.title: PRIM guidance slashed 43%; renewable project execution risk re-emerges as sector concern
bullets.body: Primoris Services cut FY26 EBITDA guidance to $275-325M from $480-500M due to cost overruns on six renewable projects, sending shares down >35% premarket. The stock has lost $7.3B in market value vs. only $270M in guidance reduction, suggesting the market sees systemic execution risk. The COO is departing following the Head of Renewables' exit, compounding investor skepticism on cost containment.
